component.name: class
component.title: Class
component.description: Invoke a method of a Java bean given by its fully qualified class name.
component.label: core,script

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

scope.description: The scope that the endpoints use when they do not set their own scope option. Singleton looks up or creates the bean once per endpoint, so it must be thread-safe. Request uses one instance per exchange, and Prototype looks up or creates the bean on each call.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

beanInfoCacheSize.label: advanced
beanInfoCacheSize.description: The maximum number of entries in the cache of bean introspection results (the methods that Camel finds by reflection on a bean class). The cache of the bean component is also used by the class component and the bean language. A value of 0 or less disables the cache.

producerIn.description: The first parameter of the method gets the body, converted to its type: a String parameter gets a Map or a POJO as its toString(), so marshal it first

producerOut.description: What the method returns, also when it returns null. A void method leaves the body unchanged

beanName.label: common
beanName.description: The name of the bean to invoke. The bean component looks it up in the Camel registry and, when no bean has that name, takes it as a class name and creates an instance. The class component takes it as the fully qualified class name.

method.label: common
method.description: The name of the method to invoke on the bean. When not set, Camel chooses the method with the bean binding rules, for example the method annotated with Handler or the method whose parameter matches the message body. Parameters can follow in parentheses, as types to choose among overloaded methods, such as foo(String), or as values to bind, such as foo(${body}, true).

scope.label: common
scope.description: How long a bean instance is reused. Singleton: the bean is looked up or created once and used for the lifetime of the endpoint, so it must be thread-safe. Request: one instance per exchange, so the bean can keep state while the same exchange calls it several times. Prototype: the bean is looked up or created on each call, and a bean from a registry such as Spring or CDI is a new instance only when that registry creates one.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

parameters.label: advanced
parameters.description: Properties to set on the bean, each given with the bean. prefix: bean.timeout=5000 calls setTimeout(5000) on the bean. The properties are set each time the bean is looked up or created, once for Singleton scope, so a bean from the registry is changed for every user of it. This is a multi-value option with prefix: bean.
